item.title: 32nd Abu Dhabi Masters R4: Antonio Viani Survives a Scare, Iniyan P. Maintains his Joint Lead
item.description: The top table clashes in round 4 of the 32nd Abu Dhabi Masters 2026 ended in peaceful draws. No big upsets happened in this round. On the top board, Iniyan Panneerselvam drew against Ahmad Ahmadzada, and now they are in joint lead with 3.5/4 points. GM Edgar Mamedov defeated GM Pranav Anand on the 4th board. The top seed, Daniil Dubov, drew against IM Usov Aleksandr E. The 5th round will start on 19th August at 5 PM Local Time/6:30 PM IST. Photos: Anmol Bhargav

item.title: Lala Shohradova Wins 2026 Asian Junior Girls Rapid, Pratitee Bordoloi Second, Prishita Gupta Third
item.description: WFM Lala Shohradova of Turkmenistan scored 6/7 points to win the 2026 Asian Junior Girls Rapid Chess Championship. WFM Pratitee Bordoloi also scored 6/7 and finished in 2nd place due to a tiebreak. FM Prishita Gupta scored 5/7 points to finish in 3rd position. Lala finished 2nd in the Blitz section too, making it her second podium finish in just 2 days. The tournament was organised on 17th and 18th August at ITC Maratha, Mumbai. Photos: Tushar Damor

item.title: Vivaan Vishal Shah Becomes 2026 Asian Junior Rapid Champion
item.description: FM Vivaan Vishal Shah scored 6/7 points to win the 2026 Asian Junior Rapid Chess Championship. Akshay Borgaonkar also scored 6/7, and he secured second place in the tournament according to tiebreak scores. IM Apoorv Kamble of India and Akhilbay Imangali of Kazakhstan tied for 3rd place, and in the tiebreak blitz match, Apoorv defeated Akhilbay 1.5-0.5 to claim 3rd place. The tournament was organised on 17th and 18th August at ITC Maratha, Mumbai. Photos: Tushar Damor

item.title: Saranya Devi Narahari Becomes 2026 Asian Junior Girls Blitz Champion
item.description: Saranya Devi Narahari scored an unbeaten 6.5/7 to win the Asian Junior Girls Blitz Chess Championship 2026. Lala Shohradova of Turkmenistan scored 6/7 points to finish in second place. Bhat Sannidhi Ramakrishna scored 5.5/7 to finish in 3rd place. Saranya drew her 2nd game and scored five consecutive wins to clinch the title. The tournament was organised on 17th August at ITC Maratha, Mumbai. Photos: Tushar Damor

item.title: Vignesh Advaith Vemula Becomes 2026 Asian Junior Blitz Champion
item.description: Vignesh Advaith Vemula scored 6/7 points to become the 2026 Asian Junior Blitz Champion. Vignesh Vemula, Viresh Sharnarthi, and Nandish VS all scored 6/7 points, but better tiebreaks helped Vignesh clinch the title. Vignesh suffered a loss in the 4th round but scored three consecutive wins and defeated GM Mayank Chakraborty in the important penultimate round. The tournament was organised on 17th August at ITC Maratha, Mumbai. Photos: Tushar Damor

item.title: 32nd Abu Dhabi Masters Round 1-3: Iniyan Panneerselvam Starts with a Perfect 3/3
item.description: The 32nd Edition of Abu Dhabi International Chess Festival started on 15th August 2026. The Masters Group is one of the strongest Swiss tournaments in Asia. Grandmaster Daniil Dubov is the top seed of the tournament, and after the completion of 3 rounds, second seed GM Iniyan Panneerselvam is leading with 3/3. IM Goutham Krishna H drew against Daniil Dubov in the 2nd round. So many talented youngsters from India and around the globe are taking part in this fantastic event. Photos: Anmol Bhargav

item.title: Cairns Cup 2026 R7: Tan Zhongyi Extends Her Lead After Beating Divya Deshmukh
item.description: Tan Zhongyi is showing her class at the 2026 Cairns Cup. In the 7th round, she defeated Divya Deshmukh with black pieces. After this win, Zhongyi is now leading with a full point, as he is on 5.5/7. Bibisara Assaubayeva also won in the 7th round against Stavroula Tsolakidou, which takes her to joint second place with Alice Lee. Koenru Humpy drew her game against Alexandra Kosteniuk. The 8th round will start on 18th August at 12 PM Local Time / 10:30 PM IST. Photos: Lennart Ootes

item.title: Sinquefield Cup 2026 R7: Javokhir Sindarov Beats Vincent Keymer To Score His First Win
item.description: In the 7th round of the 2026 Sinquefield Cup, Javokhir Sindarov defeated Vincent Keymer to register his 1st win of the tournament. All the other games between Fabiano Caruana and Praggnanandhaa, Levon Aronian and Maxime Vachier-Lagrave, and Jorden van Foreest and Sam Sevian ended in a draw. Wesley So is still in the lead after a draw against Anish Giri in the 7th round. The tournament is still wide open for anyone to grab. The 8th round will start on 18th August at 12 PM Local Time / 10:30 PM IST. Photo: Lennart Ootes

item.title: Meet Purvansh Shah: An Emerging Chess Talent who Dreams of Becoming the Youngest World Champion
item.description: Every year, thousands of children across India sit down at a chessboard for the first time. Emerging young talent Purvansh Shah was one of them, at age six, in Bangalore. What has followed since is a story built on daily habit: hours of practice, tournament after tournament, careful analysis of every loss, and a family that decided early on to treat his interest seriously. That combination has taken him from his first school-level win to the Karnataka State Schools Chess Championship (U-7 Open) title and many more.

item.title: Sinquefield Cup 2026 R6: Anish Giri Beats Jorden, Pragg Draws against Aronian
item.description: In the 6th Round of the Sinquefield Cup, there was only 1 decisive result, and it was in a Dutch clash between Anish Giri and Jorden van Foreest. Anish scored his 1st win of the tournament. With the other 4 games ending in a draw, Wesley So is still leading the tournament with 4/6. Fabiano Caruana, Vincent Keymer, R. Praggnanandhaa and Maxime Vachier Lagrave are in joint second place with 3.5/6 points. The 7th round will start on 17th August at 12 PM Local Time / 10:30 PM IST. Photo: Lennart Ootes

item.title: Cairns Cup 2026 R6: Alice Lee Scores a win against Koneru Humpy
item.description: Alice Lee defeated Koneru Humpy in the 6th round of the Cairns Cup 2026. The sixth round was played after the rest day on 15th August, and this was the only decisive result of the round. IM Carissa Yip missed a crucial chance against Bibisara Assaubayeva. Vaishali made a solid draw against Anna Muzychuk. Divya had some practical chances against Stavroula Tsolakidou. Tan Zhongyi is still leading the field with 4.5/6. The 7th round will start on 17th August at 12 PM Local Time / 10:30 PM IST. Photos: Lennart Ootes

item.title: GM Aaryan Varshney scores a perfect 9/9 to win 1st Rival of Anga Rapid Rating 2026
item.description: Grandmaster Aaryan Varshney produced a flawless performance, scoring an unbeaten 9/9 to clinch the inaugural 1st Rival of Anga International Open Rapid Rating Chess Tournament 2026 in Bhagalpur, Bihar. The two-day tournament was held on 8th and 9th August 2026 at the Bihar Agricultural University campus in Bhagalpur. The total prize fund was ₹3,00,000, with the top 3 prizes of ₹30,000, ₹20,000, and ₹15,000 along with trophies. Photos: Ajay Kumar Mishra

item.title: The Man Behind India’s 97th Grandmaster: A Conversation with Gopalakrishnan K
item.description: Every grandmaster title has two stories. The one played out on the board, and the one lived quietly off it, by the parents who skipped holidays, saved every rupee, and never once asked for credit. When Harshavardhan completed his third GM norm at the Chola Chess tournament, the cameras found him first. But just as important was the man standing a little further back, visibly emotional, finally exhaling after years of tournaments. His father, Gopalakrishnan K who is a chess trainer, former player, and by his own admission, a man who simply cannot stop loving this game. He sat down to talk about what it really takes to raise a grandmaster.

item.title: Magnus Carlsen Goes Undefeated to Retain Esports World Cup 2026 Title in Paris
item.description: Magnus Carlsen has done it again! Magnus defended his EWC Chess Title and won the Esports World Cup Chess 2026 in great style. In 20 games played, he remained undefeated and convincingly won the title. The Team Liquid star faced Denis Lazavik in the finals and won both sets with a 3-1 score to win his 2nd EWC Trophy. Magnus wins a very important 1000 Club Championship point for Team Liquid and takes home a huge sum of 250,000 USD. Photos: EWC

item.title: How did a father's promise help Rayaan become National Champion?
item.description: Rayaan Rozario recently became the National U-9 Champion. His journey to the title had an interesting story behind it. His father, Danton Rozario, works in the merchant navy and spends around six months of every year at sea. He has missed several important moments in Rayaan’s chess journey because of his job. Before the Nationals, Danton made Rayaan a promise: if he won the title, he would stay off the sea for a year and travel with him to tournaments. Rayaan went on to win the championship. Now, it was time for his father to keep his word. Read on to find out how it happened.
